practice_description.medium: Computational poetry, text generation, creative coding, writing, teaching
practice_description.practice_summary: Allison Parrish is a computational poet and programmer who uses word vectors, embedding spaces, and language models as poetic medium — treating the mathematical spaces that encode linguistic meaning as terrains to be explored, mapped, and traversed with the same intentionality a poet brings to choosing words on a page.
practice_description.methodology: Parrish works at the intersection of computational linguistics, creative writing, and critical making. Her methodology involves: (1) building custom tools and software for navigating word embedding spaces (GloVe, word2vec, and custom-trained embeddings), (2) developing novel algorithms for traversing semantic space — e.g., finding paths through embedding space that move between concepts in aesthetically interesting ways, (3) treating the topology of embedding space itself as poetic material — distances, clusters, voids, and trajectories in vector space become compositional decisions, (4) extensive critical writing and teaching articulating why this matters as poetry rather than mere technical novelty. She teaches at NYU's Interactive Telecommunications Program (ITP) and has been deeply influential in the creative coding and electronic literature communities.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Parrish is the most articulate voice on embedding space as artistic medium — her work and writing provide the conceptual vocabulary for understanding how A(DAI)'s graph-structured intelligence could become experiential territory. Her practice demonstrates that navigating semantic space is a genuinely new form of creative composition.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Partially. Parrish's poetry generated from embedding space traversal creates textual substrates — streams of language that function as ambient fields of meaning rather than fixed texts. The output is processual and navigational rather than object-like. However, the medium is primarily textual, making it more intimate and readerly than architectural.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Yes, strongly. The entire practice is relational — words and concepts are defined by their positions relative to other words in embedding space. Poetic composition involves navigating relationships between semantic clusters. The poem is a path through a relational topology. This is the most explicit example of relational composition as artistic practice in this research set.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Partially. Parrish's generative systems can produce endless variations of poetry from the same embedding space. However, the systems are typically generative-on-demand rather than continuously evolving — they produce output when invoked rather than autonomously changing over time.

works.title: Articulations
works.description: A book-length computational poem generated by sorting and interpolating between lines from the Project Gutenberg poetry corpus using phonemic and semantic similarity in embedding space. Lines from different poems across centuries are brought into proximity based on their vector representations, creating uncanny juxtapositions and continuities. Published by Counterpath Press.
works.relevance: Demonstrates how embedding space navigation can recompose a vast corpus into new meaning — directly analogous to how A(DAI)'s graph of digital arts intelligence could be traversed to produce new configurations and insights.

works.title: Compasses
works.description: An interactive web-based tool and poetic work that allows users to navigate word embedding space using directional 'compasses' — semantic vectors that define trajectories through meaning space. Users can explore how moving in directions like 'more abstract' or 'more natural' transforms language.
works.relevance: Makes embedding space navigation tangible and interactive — users directly experience the topology of semantic space. A model for how A(DAI) users might navigate the knowledge graph as an experiential rather than informational interface.

works.title: Semantic Space is Not a Space (talk/essay)
works.description: A widely cited talk and essay where Parrish critically examines the metaphor of 'space' for word embeddings — arguing that embedding spaces have properties that defy spatial intuition (non-Euclidean geometry, high dimensionality, learned biases) and that poets must grapple with these properties honestly rather than treating vector space as a transparent medium.
works.relevance: Essential theoretical reference for A(DAI). If the Sense Room involves navigating embedding/graph space, Parrish's critical analysis of what it means to move through such spaces — and what spatial metaphors conceal — is indispensable.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Parrish treats the design of traversal algorithms, similarity metrics, and compositional rules for navigating embedding space as core poetic acts. The protocol for how to move through semantic space IS the poem. She also builds and shares tools (Python libraries, Jupyter notebooks) that enable others to work with embedding spaces poetically — creating infrastructure for a practice.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Custom Python tools and libraries for poetic navigation of embedding spaces. Extensive teaching materials and Jupyter notebooks (openly shared) that serve as infrastructure for computational poetry practice. The conceptual framework articulated in her writing and teaching functions as intellectual infrastructure for the field.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Strongly commons-oriented. Parrish publishes code, Jupyter notebooks, and teaching materials openly (GitHub). Her work at ITP/NYU emphasises open pedagogy. Tools and libraries are shared for reuse. Academic and critical writing is freely accessible. The practice is embedded in open-source creative coding and electronic literature communities that value knowledge sharing.

governance_model.governance_detail: Parrish works as an independent artist-researcher-educator. Creative decisions are made independently. Teaching and community engagement happen through NYU ITP and the broader creative coding/electronic literature communities. No formal collective or organisational governance structure.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Source texts for embedding training and poetic recombination are drawn from public domain corpora (Project Gutenberg) and openly licensed datasets. No consent issues with living authors' work — Parrish is careful about the provenance of text corpora.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Solo authorship with explicit acknowledgment of computational co-authorship. Parrish is thoughtful about what the algorithm contributes versus what the poet contributes — she frames the computational system as a collaborator with its own tendencies and biases, while the artist makes curatorial and editorial decisions about what to keep, how to traverse, what constitutes a poem.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Works generate output when invoked — running the traversal algorithm produces a new poem, exploring the interactive Compasses tool produces new language in real-time. But the systems are not autonomously evolving; they await human invocation. The embedding space itself is static once trained, but the paths through it are infinite.

data_materiality.data_sources: Public domain text corpora (Project Gutenberg poetry collections), pre-trained word embedding models (GloVe, word2vec trained on large web corpora), custom-trained embeddings on specific poetry collections, phonemic transcription data for sound-similarity navigation.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Public domain (Project Gutenberg texts are out of copyright). Pre-trained embeddings (GloVe, word2vec) are trained on large web corpora by research institutions and publicly released. Self-curated poetry collections. Ethically clean — primarily public domain and openly licensed material.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Absolutely central — this is the defining feature of Parrish's practice. She is arguably the most articulate practitioner working with embedding spaces as artistic medium. Her work demonstrates: how to traverse embedding spaces with poetic intentionality, how the topology of vector space creates unexpected semantic connections, how the biases and distortions of embedding spaces are themselves poetically meaningful, and how spatial metaphors for high-dimensional representations both enable and mislead.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Primarily text-based, but Parrish has explored phonemic (sound) dimensions of embedding spaces, creating work that navigates simultaneously in semantic and sonic space. The practice is linguistically multimodal (meaning + sound + visual layout) but does not typically span image/audio/video modalities.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Works manifest as printed books (Articulations), interactive web applications (Compasses), live coding performances, and screen-based text installations. The spatial register is intimate and readerly — text on screen or page — rather than architectural or immersive. However, live performances of generative poetry create a temporal, performative spatiality.

interoperability.composability: High. Parrish's tools are Python libraries and Jupyter notebooks designed for reuse and modification. Outputs are text that can be piped into other systems. The conceptual frameworks are portable. Embedding spaces themselves are inherently composable — vectors can be combined, transformed, and fed into other processes.
interoperability.technical_openness: Open source. Code is on GitHub. Teaching materials are freely available. The practice is built on and contributes to open-source infrastructure.

technical_approach.stack: Python, Jupyter notebooks, NumPy/SciPy for vector operations, GloVe and word2vec embeddings, spaCy for NLP, custom embedding traversal algorithms, p5.js for interactive web works, openFrameworks for some earlier projects. Teaching stack includes Processing and p5.js.

network_position.scene_affiliation: Electronic literature, creative coding (Processing/p5.js community), computational linguistics, NLP/AI art, academic creative writing. Bridges the electronic literature community (ELO, Counterpath), the creative coding world (ITP/NYU, Processing Foundation), and the AI/ML art scene. Strong pedagogical influence through NYU ITP teaching.
network_position.connections: Memo Akten (shared interest in embedding spaces as artistic territory, but from opposite modalities — Parrish works with language, Akten with images). Mario Klingemann (both navigate latent/embedding spaces, but Klingemann in visual GANs, Parrish in linguistic vectors). Holly Herndon / Mat Dryhurst (shared concern with AI authorship, consent, and training data ethics).

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Parrish is the most important conceptual reference for understanding embedding space as artistic medium. She could contribute: (1) the critical vocabulary for articulating what it means to navigate graph/embedding space as an experiential practice, (2) practical algorithms for poetic traversal of high-dimensional spaces, (3) critical perspective on spatial metaphors — what they reveal and conceal about computational spaces, (4) pedagogical expertise in making these concepts accessible. Her essay 'Semantic Space is Not a Space' should be required reading for the A(DAI) team.
